title: Grade 4 CREATIVE ARTS — Premium Revision Paper #13

pages.quiz:
CREATIVE ARTS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #13
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. How is a kayamba played? (1 mark)
   A. By rubbing a bow across it
   B. By blowing into it
   C. By shaking it
   D. By plucking strings

2. In a drawing of a drum with light from the left, which part is darkest? (1 mark)
   A. Nothing is dark
   B. The side away from the light
   C. The white paper background always
   D. The side facing the light

3. To identify an instrument we give its name, its community and (1 mark)
   A. the colour of the shop
   B. the name of the shop
   C. its price
   D. how it is played

4. How high is the goal ring above the ground? (1 mark)
   A. 5 metres
   B. 1.5 metres
   C. 10 metres
   D. 3.05 metres

5. Which is a good safety rule before playing netball? (1 mark)
   A. Play on broken ground
   B. Play with long sharp nails
   C. Wear a necklace
   D. Remove rings and bracelets

6. Who stops the game with a whistle for a rule break? (1 mark)
   A. The umpire
   B. The goal keeper
   C. The spectator
   D. The shooter

7. The game restarts after each goal with (1 mark)
   A. a centre pass
   B. a throw-in from the side
   C. a jump ball
   D. a penalty kick

8. How many boxes are on the scale strip in this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. Five
   B. Ten
   C. One
   D. Two

9. Which colour is a secondary colour? (1 mark)
   A. Green
   B. Red
   C. Blue
   D. Yellow

10. Yellow mixed with blue makes (1 mark)
   A. purple
   B. green
   C. pink
   D. orange

11. Which shows neatness in a montage? (1 mark)
   A. Torn edges
   B. Clean cut edges and no glue marks
   C. Glue everywhere
   D. Loose pieces

12. A monotone line in music writing is (1 mark)
   A. a five-line staff
   B. a single line on which notes are written
   C. a colour
   D. a very loud note

13. What is a critique? (1 mark)
   A. A rude remark
   B. An honest, kind talk about someone's work
   C. A kind of drum
   D. A rest

14. Which of these four-beat patterns ends on a long note? (1 mark)
   A. taa taa taa (rest)
   B. taa ta-te taa (rest)
   C. ta-te ta-te ta-te ta-te
   D. ta-te taa ta-te taa

15. The sol-fa syllable d is pronounced (1 mark)
   A. day
   B. dah
   C. dee
   D. doh

16. Which tune ends on the home note? (1 mark)
   A. d r m r d
   B. r m r m
   C. d r m r
   D. m r m r

17. Which is a safety rule for sprint races? (1 mark)
   A. Push to get ahead
   B. Never push or trip another runner
   C. Run in any lane
   D. Run backwards

18. How far apart are the hands placed at the start? (1 mark)
   A. Shoulder-width apart
   B. One on each side of the track
   C. As far as possible
   D. Touching each other

19. At the set position, the hips are (1 mark)
   A. on the ground
   B. lower than the knees
   C. behind the line only
   D. a little higher than the shoulders

20. If your head drops back with a strain in the crab balance, you should (1 mark)
   A. keep the head in line and look gently up
   B. throw it back further
   C. close your mouth tight
   D. hold your breath

21. A good sequence has (1 mark)
   A. no order
   B. a clear start, smooth middle and controlled finish
   C. only noise
   D. only jumps

22. In a crab balance, your fingers point (1 mark)
   A. away from your feet
   B. behind your back
   C. up to the sky
   D. towards your feet

23. Funeral songs are usually (1 mark)
   A. about sports
   B. loud only
   C. fast and joyful
   D. slow and sad

24. How should you behave when the anthem is sung? (1 mark)
   A. Run around
   B. Stand straight and quietly
   C. Talk to friends
   D. Play games

25. The mood of a song is (1 mark)
   A. its length in metres
   B. its price
   C. the feeling it gives
   D. the name of the composer

26. Which of these can also take digital photographs? (1 mark)
   A. Broom
   B. Drum
   C. Tablet
   D. Xylophone

27. Which is a digital device for photography? (1 mark)
   A. Ruler
   B. Kayamba
   C. Recorder
   D. Smartphone

28. Which photo should be kept? (1 mark)
   A. One with a finger on the lens
   B. One with good light and a clear centre of interest
   C. One that is dark and blurred
   D. One taken by accident

29. A photograph is also called a (1 mark)
   A. montage
   B. photo
   C. drum
   D. stave

30. How should you hold the recorder? (1 mark)
   A. Pointing at your face
   B. Pointing down and away from your body at an angle
   C. Above your head
   D. Flat on your lap

31. On the staff, the note A sits (1 mark)
   A. above the staff
   B. below the staff
   C. in the space between lines 2 and 3
   D. on line 1

32. Why is it called the mushroom float? (1 mark)
   A. It tastes good
   B. The back at the surface looks like the top of a mushroom
   C. It grows
   D. It is very tall

33. What happens if you lift your head during a glide? (1 mark)
   A. Nothing
   B. You fly
   C. You go faster
   D. Your legs sink

34. Counting steps and jumps in animal games links to (1 mark)
   A. Mathematics
   B. Geography maps
   C. Foreign languages only
   D. Chemistry

35. What happens when the hawk tags the last chick? (1 mark)
   A. The hen goes home
   B. The chick becomes the hawk
   C. The hawk sleeps
   D. The game ends forever

36. To analyse a work of art means to (1 mark)
   A. ignore it
   B. throw it away
   C. paint over it
   D. look closely at its parts to understand it

37. In a folk song, the soloist (1 mark)
   A. is the audience
   B. is silent
   C. leads and sings the call
   D. plays the drum only

38. A good sportsperson (1 mark)
   A. quits
   B. congratulates winners and encourages losers
   C. cheats
   D. argues with the referee

39. Works on display should be kept away from (1 mark)
   A. walls
   B. other pictures
   C. shelves
   D. water, direct sun and dust

40. Sportsmanship means (1 mark)
   A. hitting
   B. cheating to win
   C. teasing others
   D. being fair and kind in sports

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Give four ways in which gymnastics helps the body. (4 marks)

42. Why is it important to keep the right posture during a sprint? (3 marks)

43. Explain how to analyse a folk song performance using its components. (5 marks)

44. Describe how to make an overhead pass. (3 marks)

45. Describe the roles of the soloist, the chorus and the instrumentalists in a folk song. (3 marks)

46. Explain how the elongated start is different from the medium start. (4 marks)

47. Describe how to paint a fruit so that it looks round using colour value. (4 marks)

48. How should you give feedback on a friend's photograph? (3 marks)

49. How can an elder help you to learn indigenous games? (2 marks)

50. State the jobs of the lens, the screen and the battery of a camera. (3 marks)

51. List four steps of the medium start. (4 marks)

52. Why is it important not to share a recorder before cleaning it? (3 marks)

53. State two ways of playing percussion instruments. (2 marks)

54. Describe the steps for painting a picture of one object that shows colour value. (5 marks)

55. How should we behave towards the national flag? (3 marks)

56. Why are funeral songs usually slow and sad? (3 marks)

57. Describe how to do the mushroom float. (3 marks)

58. Why should you never point a camera directly at the sun? (3 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #13 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — By shaking it
   The kayamba is a shaker with seeds inside. You shake it back and forth.

2. B — The side away from the light
   Shadows fall on the side away from the light, so it is darker.

3. D — how it is played
   Identifying uses name, community and method of playing.

4. D — 3.05 metres
   The netball goal ring is 3.05 metres high.

5. D — Remove rings and bracelets
   Jewellery can hurt you and others.

6. A — The umpire
   Umpires control the game and blow the whistle.

7. A — a centre pass
   The game restarts with a centre pass, and the teams take turns.

8. A — Five
   The strip is divided into five equal boxes.

9. A — Green
   Green is made from yellow and blue.

10. B — green
   Yellow and blue give green.

11. B — Clean cut edges and no glue marks
   Neatness means careful cutting and pasting.

12. B — a single line on which notes are written
   On a monotone we write the rhythm on one line.

13. B — An honest, kind talk about someone's work
   A critique gives fair comments in a respectful way.

14. D — ta-te taa ta-te taa
   Only the first ends on a crotchet (taa).

15. D — doh
   The syllable d is doh.

16. A — d r m r d
   Only d r m r d ends on d.

17. B — Never push or trip another runner
   Pushing or tripping can hurt people.

18. A — Shoulder-width apart
   Hands are about shoulder-width apart.

19. D — a little higher than the shoulders
   On set the hips lift slightly above the shoulders.

20. A — keep the head in line and look gently up
   Keep the head in line with the body.

21. B — a clear start, smooth middle and controlled finish
   Good sequences are planned and controlled.

22. D — towards your feet
   In the crab position, hands are behind you with fingers pointing to the feet.

23. D — slow and sad
   They comfort families and remember the person.

24. B — Stand straight and quietly
   An anthem is sung with respect.

25. C — the feeling it gives
   Mood is the feeling of a song, such as joy or calm.

26. C — Tablet
   Many tablets have cameras.

27. D — Smartphone
   A smartphone has a camera lens and digital memory.

28. B — One with good light and a clear centre of interest
   Good photographs are well lit and clear.

29. B — photo
   Photo is short for photograph.

30. B — Pointing down and away from your body at an angle
   The recorder is held pointing down at about 45 degrees.

31. C — in the space between lines 2 and 3
   A is in the space between G and B.

32. B — The back at the surface looks like the top of a mushroom
   The rounded back at the top looks like a mushroom cap.

33. D — Your legs sink
   Lifting the head lowers the legs.

34. A — Mathematics
   Counting is a maths skill.

35. B — The chick becomes the hawk
   Roles change so everyone plays.

36. D — look closely at its parts to understand it
   Analysing means studying the parts.

37. C — leads and sings the call
   The soloist starts or leads.

38. B — congratulates winners and encourages losers
   Fair play and respect.

39. D — water, direct sun and dust
   Water, sun and dust can damage works.

40. D — being fair and kind in sports
   It includes following rules and respecting others.

SECTION B
----
41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Makes muscles stronger; improves flexibility; improves balance and coordination; exercises the heart and lungs; builds confidence. Any four.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: It keeps the body moving forward in a straight line. It saves energy and helps speed. It prevents pain or injury.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid reason.

43. (5 marks)
   Answer: Say the community of origin, the type or occasion, the message and mood, the roles of the soloist, chorus and instrumentalists, and the instruments used.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of five components.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Lift the ball above the head with both hands and elbows slightly bent. Step forward and throw from behind the head, flicking wrists and fingers so the ball goes over the defender.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the start, 1 mark for the throw, 1 mark for going over the defender.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: The soloist leads, the chorus answers and repeats, the instrumentalists play instruments to keep the beat.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each role.

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: The rear knee is placed further back, level with the heel of the front foot. The feet are further apart. The push is longer and stronger but may feel less steady.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid difference or explanation, up to 4.

47. (4 marks)
   Answer: Draw the outline. Paint the main colour. Add a lighter tone on the side facing the light and a darker tone on the side away from the light. Blend the edges and add a shadow.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: Say what you like first, comment on light and centre of interest, and suggest one improvement politely.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

49. (2 marks)
   Answer: The elder can teach you the games and songs of the community and share their stories.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: The lens lets light in; the screen shows the view and photos; the battery gives power.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

51. (4 marks)
   Answer: Front foot about one and a half foot lengths behind the line; kneel on the rear knee level with the middle of the front foot; hands behind the line shoulder-width apart; on set, lift the hips a little above the shoulders.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: Germs from the mouth can spread illnesses such as colds through the mouthpiece.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for germs, 1 mark for the mouth or mouthpiece, 1 mark for spreading illness.

53. (2 marks)
   Answer: Striking and shaking. Scraping is also correct.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

54. (5 marks)
   Answer: Choose an object and place it near a window. Draw the outline lightly. Mix the main colour and paint the object. Add a lighter tone on the lit side and a darker tone on the shadow side. Blend the edges and add a shadow, then let it dry.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of five clear steps.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: Do not let it touch the ground, do not write on it, keep it clean and not torn, and stand still and quiet when it is raised.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid point.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: They comfort the family and remember the person who has died, so the mood is calm and serious.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid point.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: In shallow water take a breath and put the face in. Bend the knees and hug them to the chest with the chin tucked. The back rises to the surface. Hold for a few seconds.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: It can hurt your eyes and the strong light will spoil the picture.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for eyes, 1 mark for picture, 1 mark for explanation.
